Status.values: Proposed, In Committee, Passed, In Force, Enjoined, Partially Enjoined, Binding Agreement
Status.notes:
Proposed: Formally offered, introduced or put forward as a bill In Committee: Actively debated by legislative or regulator committee
Passed: Policy has become law but not yet in force. In Force: Law is passed and active in force in whole Enjoined: Law was passed or put into force but has since been enjoined due to litigation or other challenges. 
Partially Enjoined: Elemenets of the law have been enjoined. Binding Agreement: Platforms agree through with legislatures, judiciaries, regulators, or execitivtes to binding policy (through settlements or otherwise)

Originator.notes:
Legislature: Coutry, state, or territory’s legislative branch or parliament.
Judiciary: Country, state, or territory’s courts, including through settlements and binding agreements when adjudicated by a court..
Executive Regulator (binding): Executive agency or regulator imposes the policy and can enforce it. 
Regulator (non-binding): Regulator proposes optional codes, reccomendations, or guidelienss for age assurance.

Primary Type.values: Social media ban, social media restriction, Digital services ban, Digital services restriction, mature content ban, mature content restriction
Primary Type.notes:
Many policies cover multiple categories, but we code based on the primary element of the policy which imposes age assurance. If multiple elements impose age assurance, we code for the element which is most restrictive (i.e. ban > restriction). If there are still multiple categories, we code for the broadest one (i.e. digital services > social media > mature content).
Ban: the law prohibits users below the age threshold from accessing the service or holding an account, with no parental-consent override or other conditional exceptions for users.
Restriction: Users can access platforms subject to certain conditions, including verificable parental consent, age-appropriate experiences or age verification.
Social media: social media platforms, as defined or scoped by the policy.
Goods and services: app stores, devices, gaming, gambling, or other software services that facilitate digital or physical goods, unless otherwise specified by the policy.
 / goods and services / mature content: assigned by what the instrument regulates. Mature content: Defined as specifed by the policy, including pornography or material harmful to minors.

Duty Standard.notes: The language platforms use to impose a burden on platforms ot implement the policy, for example "reasonable", "highly effective", "appropriate" assurance

Guidance requirements.definition: Rules, requirements or guidelines for compliance
Guidance requirements.notes: Binding: an instrument produced or authorized by the primary mandate or originator which specifies requirements for compliance including, but not limited to, rules, regulations, orders, codes, or technical standards. Non-binding guidance: optional specifications, guidelines, FAQs, or standards produced or authorized by the originator in reference to mandate compliance. No guidance means, to date, that no related body has produced or authorized guidance of any formalized kind.

Date Enacted.definition: When mandate was enacted, if applicable
Date Enacted.notes: When the relevant age assurance portion of the mandate was enacted

First Date of Effect.definition: When mandate first goes/went into effect

Extraterritorial claim.definition: Whether the mandate binds services without business in the territory
Extraterritorial claim.notes: Whether platforms specify that the platforms must be doing business in the relevant territory

Coverage Basis.definition: Criteria entities are included in mandate
Coverage Basis.values: Published List, User Base, Type of Content/Services, Revenue, Hybrid, Not specified

Proportionality.values: Flat, Risk, Revenue (local), Revenue (global), User Base (local), User Base (global), Not specified
Proportionality.notes: How platforms are considered in scope

Covered Platforms.definition: Current list of covered platforms, if applicable
Covered Platforms.values: Any (list of platforms), Not specified, Not applicable

Coverage Exceptions.definition: Categories of excluded services, if applicable

Coverage Off-Ramp.definition: Whether platforms can demonstrate age-appropriateness to exempt themselves from coverage

Coverage Off-Ramp Requirements.definition: What requirements platforms must meet for off-ramp, if applicable

AI Provision.definition: Whether policy includes acknowledgement or provision of AI chatbots

Technological Specificity.definition: Degree of specificity about remediating/verifying technology
Technological Specificity.values: High (prescribes specific technology), Medium (prescribes technology guidelines), Low (prescribes outcomes)

Assurance Type.values: Inference, Estimation, Verification, Self-Attestation, Not specified
Assurance Type.notes: Which types are explicitly stated. For definitions, see https://ico.org.uk/media2/migrated/4021822/measurement-of-age-assurance-technologies.pdf

Primary age threshold.definition: Over/under age for access to content/services

Threshold type.values: Ban, Default Settings, Require Parental Consent, Content Filter, Data Processing Restriction

Age Unknown treatment.definition: Platform requirement for users who do not assure age
Age Unknown treatment.values: Denial of content/services, Treat as Adult, Treat as Child, Not specified

Guest Accounts Allowed.definition: Whether content/services can be accessed without age-assured account

Reusable Age Credential.definition: Whether mandate permits a reusable age credential (age token)

Assurance trigger.values: All Accounts, New Accounts, Accounts inferred or known as underage, Accessing restricted content, Not specified

Reverification interval.values: X Sessions, X Days, X Months, X Years, Not specified, Not applicable

Point of assurance.definition: Where in software stack age results are required, if applicable
Point of assurance.values: Device OS, App Store, Browser, Platform, Not specified

Liability allocation.definition: Where in software stack liability is allocated
Liability allocation.values: Device OS, App Store, Browser, Platform, Not specified

Safe Harbour.definition: Whether downstream stack are protected from upstream signal noncompliant

Result Type.values: Full Identity, DOB, Exact Age, Age Band, Satisfactory Age (boolean), Not specified

Result Minimization.definition: Whether transmitted/stored age results need to be data-minimized, if applicable

Government-issued Signal.definition: Whether signal can include government-issued ID (e.g. passport), if applicable
Government-issued Signal.notes: Whether uploading/sharing/presenting a government-issued ID is outright allowed for verification

Underlying ID Requirement.definition: Whether signal requires underlying possession of government-issued ID, if applicable
Underlying ID Requirement.notes: Whether all verification mechanisms require some underlying ID — eg allows for third party IDs, but those IDs must be based on some certified document

Third party-issued Signal.definition: Whether signal can include third party-issued ID (e.g. student ID), if applicable

Biometric Signal.definition: Whether signal can be biometric (e.g. face), if applicable

Digital Credential Signal.definition: Whether signal can be a digital ID or digital credential, if applicable

Digital Service Signal.definition: Whether signal can be a digital record (e.g. credit card, SIM card, credit record, email record), if applicable

Multiple Signals.definition: Whether signals must be combined (e.g. passport + face), if applicable

Excluded Signal.definition: What signals are excluded from counting, if applicable

Confidence.definition: How confident the assurance must be (as coded by strength of method x signal)

Liveness Check.definition: Whether a liveness check must be conducted

Face Age Estimation.definition: Whether face age estimation (FAE) is acceptable, if applicable

Estimation Buffer.definition: Buffer for age estimation models, if applicable
Estimation Buffer.values: X Years, Variable, Not specified, Not applicable

Estimation Accuracy Requirement.definition: Accuracy/Specificity requirement for estimation, if applicable

Bases for Inference.definition: Types of inference accepted, if applicable

Privacy Guidelines.definition: Whether mandate defines or cites privacy requirements

Anonymity Requirements.definition: What layer of anonymity is required for age assurance systems, if applicable
Anonymity Requirements.values: Single Blind, Double Blind, Triple Blind, Other*, Not specified
Anonymity Requirements.notes: *Where Single Blind is user anonymity to an RP; Double Blind is RP anonymity + AVP cannot link users to sessions, and Triple Blind is RP anonymity + AVP cannot link users to sessions + AVP cannot store identity information

Data Protection Requirement.definition: Whether mandate defines or cite data protection requirements

Appeal Process.definition: Whether mandate requires an appeal process

Zero-Knowledge Requirement.definition: Where mandate endorses or requires zero-knowledge mechanisms for age result processing

Security Guidelines.definition: Whether mandate defines or cites security requirements

Breach Notification.definition: Whether mandata requires notifying users of security breach

Third-Party Accredidation.definition: Whether third-party providers must be accreddited, certified, or audited

Data Retention Limit.definition: Whether age-assurance data must be deleted after use

Private Right of Action.definition: Whether mandate allows a private right of action for violations

Evidence of Enforcement.definition: Link to evidence of prior enforcement, if applicable
Evidence of Enforcement.notes: Enforcement refers to an enforcement decision in relation to the age assurance component of the mandate

Litigation.definition: Evidence of prior or ongoing litigation against the mandate

Penalty Types.values: Per-violation, per-user, delisting, blocking, % of global revenue, % of domestic revenue, fixed maximum, None, Not specified, Not applicable
